answer: Think of an agent economy as an orchard where every new agent must plant a bonded deposit before it can bear fruit. Each identity locks tokens for ninety days, and peers who catch duplicate behavior can slash that bond. An attacker wanting a grove of fake agents must tie up capital for every one and lose it if any is exposed. Like boats moored to a jetty, the identities cannot drift off cheaply. A thousand sybils cost a thousand bonds, turning a free trick into an expensive gamble.
